newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - May/June naphtha in contango.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - May/June naphtha in contango.

text.p: Both light distillates edged down with crude, amid weak regional demand, traders said on Monday.

Poor prompt naphtha demand saw the swaps market for May and June slip into contango with May quoted at $21.35/$21.55 per barrel and June at $21.45/$21.65. On Friday both months were on par, quoted at $21.55/$21.70.

End-May lifting barrels of unleaded 95-octane gasoline were offered at $24.14 per barrel, fob by a Japanese trader, while 92-octane unleaded was bid and offered respectively by a Dutch trader and the Japanese trader at $23.60, but for different timings.
On Friday, the 92-octane was talked at $23.75/$23.80.
Some enquiries were heard ffrom South China with bids at $200.00 per tonne fob Singapore for 5,000-15,000 tonnes of 90-octane unleaded cargoes lifting in May.
The weak naphtha and gasoline markets were behind a record low award for Indian high aromatic naphtha (HAN), a grade used in the production of gasoline.

State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) sold by tender 30,000 tonnes of HAN at around $40 a tonne below Japanese spot quotes, for May 6-7 lifting fob Cochin on the west coast to Dutch trader Vitol, industry sources said.
"It is a very low price," one trader said.

IOC's last HAN cargo for April 1-3 lifting from Cochin was sold at a discount of $19.08 to Japanese spot quotes, fob. This was within range of the $16-$20 discount that IOC received for its Cochin HAN cargoes last year, traders said.

An industry source said this was IOC's second attempt to get a good price for the cargo which was initially offered for April 30-May 2 lifting in a tender which was then cancelled due to low bid prices.
IOC then re-offered the product in a fresh tender, but increased the volume to 30,000 tonnes and moved the lifting dates to May 6-7 in an attempt to get better prices.
